decisions.reason: B remains close to the core decorative range, and although its limited prominence suggests results may be around rather than clearly above aspiration, portfolio breadth and some organisational slack support keeping it under review for another year.
C matches the firm's curtain business and adds a valued flame-retardant function for project customers, so its performance is likely to stay above aspiration and justify retention.

D builds on existing design and material capabilities, and even if demand appears moderate, its adjacency to the established collection makes continued offering more likely than reallocation of resources now.

E looks the most niche and weakly signaled product, and after two selling seasons a likely shortfall against rising aspirations makes shifting its resources to stronger lines and new development the more plausible choice.

F is a recent launch with strong website support and a versatile upholstery-and-curtain positioning, so boundedly rational management would usually allow more time for learning before considering withdrawal.
